maria: Heads-up — while profiling the KV-cache hotpath on the prod-sim node with nsys 23.8 + CUPTI, I’m seeing intermittent kernel eviction and large tail latency spikes for small batches. Traces show missing cupti activity records for several kernels and a bunch of ioctls that look like probes. Attaching quick repro and logs below. Anyone seen sampling gaps like this on driver 520.61?

devon: which exact nsys flags did you run? also which container runtime & rootless mapping? sometimes uidmap perms make CUPTI fail silently.

maria: ran: `nsys profile --stats=true --sample=none --capture-range=cudaDriverApi --output=kvhot-nsys ./run_inference.sh` (we toggled --sample to try both). Container is rootless podman with uidmap 1000:0-65535. Driver on host: 520.61, kernel 5.15. CUPTI logs: `CUPTI_ERROR: 0x00000016 - CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_DEVICE` and repeated `failed to get activity records` in the nsys stdout.

alex: fwiw we hit similar when nsys attempted to open /dev/nvidia* from an unprivileged user — the ioctl fallthrough causes the device to return EACCES and the runtime sometimes reschedules kernels while profiling hooks are in flight. Try running nsys with `--capture-range=none` and `--trace=nvtx` to minimize intrusive capture, then compare. Also try the CUPTI LD_PRELOAD workaround: `LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcupti.so nsys profile ...` (worked around missing symbol for us).

josh: we saw KV cache miss spikes too — profiling seemed to reorder some kernel launches (esp small GEMM kernels) so they ended up on different compute queues and got preempted, raising latency. The perfetto kernel timeline shows sequences like: `cudaLaunchKernel -> ioctl(DRM) -> scheduler stall -> kernel requeue`. The interesting bit: with nsys 23.10 + driver 525.x the cuptiActivity callbacks were populated consistently. With 23.8 + 520.x we had gaps.

maria: snippets from nsys stderr: ```
[2026-12-02T14:22:08Z] CUPTI: warning: Activity buffer overflow, skipping records
[2026-12-02T14:22:09Z] ERROR: cuptiActivityPush: CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED (22)
[2026-12-02T14:22:09Z] ioctl(0xC0206421, NV_DEVICE_IOCTL_SOME_PROBE, ...) = -1 EACCES
```

alex: also check NVML/CUDA driver ABI mismatch. nsys bundles a CUPTI shim, and mismatched libcuda or driver ABI can produce these exact symptoms. Quick check: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv` and `strings /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so | grep ABI`. If mismatched, either upgrade driver or use the nsys release matched to the driver.

devon: workaround we used in staging: (1) run profiler from a privileged helper pod that mounts /dev/nvidia* with correct uid, (2) set `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` to a single GPU to reduce cross-GPU ioctl noise, (3) bump to nsys 23.10. That removed most of the CUPTI gaps for us.

perf-bot: nsys run ended with EXIT_CODE=1, last stderr: "cuptiActivityPush: CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED (22)" (job id: 2026-12-02-kvhot-87).

maria: Thanks — trying privileged helper + nsys 23.10 + driver 525.78 tomorrow. I’ll upload perfetto+nsys timelines so we can compare kernel queueing differences and batching heuristics impact. cc @devon @alex :thumbsup:

josh: if you can collect a short perfetto capture too (5–10s around a hot batch) that’ll make hotspot mapping much easier. I’ll diff the KV cache miss traces once you upload. :mag_right:
